basis: Intellectual disability defines the syndrome; skeletal abnormalities occur in 30-79%. Eye and ear morphology alone does not establish functional damage; kidney abnormalities are under 30%.
Thymic epithelial carcinoma has no organ axis. Lung/liver metastases reported in ~30% collectively do not establish involvement of either individual organ in >=30%.
Congenital skeletal myopathy; persistent ptosis in 12/14 and ophthalmoparesis in 3/4 support ocular involvement. Peripheral neuropathy is occasional; respiratory weakness is muscular.
Persistent inflammation of the larynx, part of the airway; an infectious or autoimmune mechanism is not required.
Cutaneous melanoma subtype arising in skin.
Diffuse inflammation of the corneal stroma; no specific infectious or autoimmune cause is established by this concept.
Cutaneous T-cell lymphoma directly infiltrates skin and causes elastolysis. Renal involvement and hypercalcemia are occasional; associated Hodgkin lymphoma is a separate disease.
Germ-cell neoplasm of the ovary, a reproductive organ; germ-cell origin does not establish endocrine disease.
Defined by extensive brain malformations, severe developmental impairment and optic nerve hypoplasia.
Isolated spermatogenic failure with globozoospermia and infertility; reproductive dysfunction without established endocrine disease.
Carcinoma arising from the exocrine pancreatic ductal epithelium.
Grade II glial neoplasm arising in the central nervous system.
Acute myeloid leukemia directly involves marrow and blood cells; no additional organ involvement meeting the threshold is established.
Cerebellar and autonomic neurodegeneration define MSA-C. Bladder dysfunction, orthostasis and disordered breathing reflect neural dysfunction rather than direct injury to those organs.
Developmental impairment and metopic craniosynostosis define the syndrome. Cardiac and anorectal malformations are reported without evidence of >=30% frequency.
Skeletal dysplasia defined by calvarial lesions, bone fragility and vertebral/metaphyseal abnormalities.
EEF1A2-related developmental and epileptic encephalopathy causes seizures and developmental impairment; no metabolic disorder is established by the supplied phenotype.
Substance dependence is a psychiatric condition; intoxication, withdrawal and potential organ complications are not defining direct organ disease.
Congenital skeletal myopathy; cardiomyopathy occurs in 2/4 reported patients. Reduced vital capacity can reflect respiratory muscle weakness and does not establish direct lung disease.
Carcinoma originating in epithelial cells of the renal collecting ducts.
Ischemic injury directly affects the small or large intestine. A primary vascular lesion is not required, and underlying vascular diseases are separate conditions.
Usually benign cutaneous neoplasm arising from eccrine sweat glands.
FGFR1-related Pfeiffer syndrome is defined by craniosynostosis and broad digits. Additional damaging ocular, auditory or airway involvement is not established at >=30% for this subtype.
Defined by pigmentary abnormalities, ocular disease and deafness. Dental abnormalities, including macrodontia and delayed eruption, occur in 80-99%; teeth belong to gastrointestinal.
Inherited congenital pendular nystagmus defines an ocular motor disorder; no independent structural or developmental CNS disease is established.
